Hapless

/HAP-lis/ - the stress falls on HAP · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Hapless means unlucky.

The hapless street magician drew his first real crowd just as a gust scattered his cards into the fountain.

Worked Example

Every festival the hapless food-truck owner booked was rained out, and at the summer's one sunny fair her generator died before noon. Nobody could name a thing she had done wrong; luck simply refused to take her side.

Hapless means dogged by misfortune — and, crucially, blameless. A careless person earns their disasters; a hapless one just keeps receiving them, which is why the word carries pity with a small, kind smile inside it.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

unlucky: suffering a bad break or two; hapless misfortune follows a person around

luckless: equally out of luck, but drier — without the note of pity

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

charmed: as if protected by luck itself

favored: smiled on — the breaks always seem to land your way

Where it sits · how relentless and final the misfortune is — unlucky → hapless → doomed

unlucky vs. hapless: Unlucky is milder than hapless — one bad break is unlucky; hapless suggests misfortune has adopted you.

doomed vs. hapless: Doomed goes further than hapless — a hapless traveler misses the train, while a doomed venture is certain to end in disaster.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — hap

Root — hap: luck, chance (Old Norse happ)

Suffix — -less

Suffix — -less: without

Put it together

Put it together: Hap (luck) + -less (without) = without luck, plain as that. The same little luck-word hides inside happen (what chance brings), perhaps (by chance), and even happy — which first meant 'favored by luck.' A hapless person is standing outside that whole lucky family, in the rain.

Use the root in a new word: mishap

Use the root in a new word: mishap: The move went smoothly except for one mishap: a box of glasses met the staircase.

Word Choice

neutral, gently comic

Hapless pities the chronically unlucky with half a smile — the hapless intern, the hapless picnickers. It assigns no blame: misfortune just keeps arriving. 'Unlucky' fits a single bad break; hapless suggests a career of them. Unlike its unit-mate forlorn, a hapless person isn't abandoned or hopeless — just permanently rained on.
